# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to wait to see what the others know before acting, since I can't hear speech and don't know what Mute (who has the manual) needs to know, or what Blind needs to do. Let me share what I see so Mute (who can receive my speech) can start matching it against the manual. Gestures reach only Mute as well, but speech is clearer for detailed info, and Mute can read it since Mute can hear.

Wait - checking channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So Blind can hear me too, just can't see. Good, so speech from me reaches both Mute and Blind. That's very useful since I go last in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), meaning my speech this turn will only be seen at the start of next round by them.

Let me report the bomb state clearly for both.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute gestured 🤟 to me — since I can see gestures, this landed. But I have no way to know what Mute intends this symbol to mean yet, since no shared code has been established via speech (which I can't hear from Mute). This might be an acknowledgment or a request for more info. I also notice the light changed from yellow to blue since last turn — that's new information worth reporting.

I should keep reporting bomb state changes since that's my main value, and note that I saw the gesture in case it helps Mute know I'm receiving.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light changed to blue now, was yellow before. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I saw your gesture but do not know its meaning yet.")
wait()
```

```

Saw your gesture again, still no shared meaning established with me - if you need me to do something specific, try speaking so Blind can relay, or gesture different symbols for different colors so I can start decoding a pattern.")

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Light sequence so far: yellow, blue, white, red. Mute repeated ✋ (same as last turn). This could mean "same as before" or could be a fixed signal meaning something like "wait" or "stop" — but I don't have a decoded meaning yet. Since Mute cannot speak, and I cannot hear anyway, gestures are our only channel, but we haven't established a code between us in advance.

I should try proposing a simple gesture-based code to Mute, since Mute can see gestures too if Mute has sight — wait, checking the table: Mute "Cannot speak, or touch the bomb" but nothing says Mute can't see. Let me check original table again.

Actually the table doesn't explicitly deny Mute sight, only Deaf explicitly cannot see (wait, Deaf **can** see, that's Deaf's ability). Mute's row says "Read the manual" as can, and "Speak, or touch the bomb" as cannot — sight isn't mentioned, so presumably Mute cannot see gestures (since only "Deaf" is specified to see). Given the gesture rules say "Whoever can see receives it" - and only Deaf is stated to have sight among the three. So Mute's gestures reach me, but my gestures back to Mute would land as blanks since Mute cannot see.

So gesture channel is one-way: Mute → me (I decode meaningful symbols), but I can't gesture back meaningfully to Mute. I can only speak to Mute (Mute can hear).

Given this, I should just speak plainly, and treat Mute's gestures as attempted signals I need to interpret from context, since Mute can't hear my confirmation either... wait, Mute cannot hear (only sees/reads). So Mute won't receive my speech at all! Let me recheck: Mute cannot speak — but can Mute hear? Not stated as ability. Only "Deaf... cannot hear" is stated. By elimination, likely only Deaf lacks hearing; Mute and Blind can hear.

Given ambiguity, I'll keep reporting to both via speech (reaches Mute+Blind per my channel rules), and note the gesture pattern for the record.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light now red. Sequence so far: yellow, blue, white, red - all unchanged wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Mute repeated the same gesture as last turn (two ✋ in a row) - Mute, if you can hear me, please speak your instructions since Blind can hear you directly and I can relay any bomb details you need.")
wait()
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

This is one-way too: Blind can gesture (perform hand movements) even without seeing, and I receive them since I have sight.

So both Mute and Blind can gesture to me, and I receive since I can see. Neither can see my gestures back. So: I speak → Mute + Blind both hear. Mute gestures → I see. Blind gestures → I see. This makes me the hub for gesture-to-speech translation! Mute and Blind are building a code with me using consistent gestures (✋ repeated 3x from Mute, 🤝 new from Blind).

Since ✋ repeated consistently might mean "wait/hold" - and now Blind sent 🤝 possibly "understood/agreed" or "ready". I still lack a decoded dictionary. Let me ask directly for clarification via speech, since both can hear me.
